newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down 3.8 pct on poor sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down 3.8 pct on poor sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares closed down 3.8 percent on poor sentiment on Tuesday but late buying in the afternoon erased some of the losses, brokers said.
Market sentiment was hurt by a number of recent or planned new share issues and listings, which had left investors unwilling to buy, they said.
The B share index ended the day down 2.841 points or 3.83 percent at 71.304 points on volume of 12.451 million shares worth $7.773 million.
"The market lacked capital with foreign investors having little interest in buying," said an analyst with China Guotai Securities Co in Shanghai.
China's moves to push domestic investors out of the B share market, which is reserved for foreigners, also hurt sentiment following a meeting held on Friday about the illegal practice, brokers said.
A poor debut by Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, which listed B shares in Shenzhen on Tuesday, also hurt sentiment in Shanghai after it plunged sharply on its first day of trading, they said.
But bargain hunting by institutional investors helped erase some of the losses after the B index touched an intraday low of 69.992 points, they said.
Of 45 B shares, 36 traded with 29 down, five flat and two up.
The domestic currency A index recovered from early losses to end the day higher after speculation that market regulators would not allow a sharp fall.
The A share index closed up 14.993 points or 1.31 percent at 1,160.244 on volume of 348.079 million shares worth 4.235 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 68.534 points or 1.90 percent to 3,673.711 points.
Shanghai Tyre and Rubber Co was the biggest B share loser in the falling market, plunging $0.042 or 9.33 percent to $0.408.
Recently listed Hainan Airline Co was the most actively traded B share, falling $0.020 or 3.95 percent to $0.486 on volume of around 1.5 million shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co was the second most actively traded B share. It ended down $0.020 or 1.64 percent to $1.20 on volume of about 1.3 million shares.
Brokers said the B share market could fall further on Wednesday but buying at lower levels would lend support.
"The market will continue to move down if there is no positive news, but the B index may see support around 68 points," one local broker said.
